title: CTEs, Subqueries, and Set Operations: Visual Guide
outline: Title: CTEs, Subqueries, and Set Operations: Visual Guide

1. The Grain Pipeline | a four-stage WITH pipeline where each stage can be made the final SELECT, showing its rows and what one row means | a CTE gives every grain change a name and an inspectable contract, which is where fan-out and illegal-column mistakes become visible

2. Naming A Result | CTE, view and temp table compared on scope, storage, indexability and cost, plus a CTE referenced twice shown inlined and materialised | a CTE is statement-scoped and the engine chooses whether to inline or materialise it, so exactly-once needs a temp table rather than a hope

3. Correlated Or Not | the same AVG(score) filter written uncorrelated and correlated, with the inner query's actual input shown for the tapped outer row | an uncorrelated subquery is computed once and a correlated one is logically re-evaluated per outer row, and the test is simply whether an outer column appears inside the parentheses

4. The Cost Of Per-Row | a slider over outer-set size comparing an unindexed correlated scan, a pre-aggregate-then-join, and indexed keyed probes | correlation is only dangerous when a large outer set meets inner work that is not a cheap keyed probe, and which rewrite wins flips as the outer set grows

5. Duplicate Semantics | two overlapping exports combined with UNION ALL and UNION, with a switch that adds the score column to the projection | UNION removes duplicates across the complete selected tuple rather than the business key, so adding one differing column makes the duplicate reappear and keyed precedence needs an explicit stage
